rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice in mathematical expressions such as 二加二等於四.

example.jyutping: ji6 gaa1 ji6 dang2 jyu1 sei3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose term for the literal plus sign symbol (+).
Use this in spoken arithmetic when referring to the plus operator rather than explicitly naming the written symbol.

example.jyutping: ji6 gaa1 saam1 dang2 jyu1 ng5

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken connector before an additional reason or fact.

example.english: I’m not going jogging today, plus it’s raining.
example.traditional: 我今日唔去跑步，仲要落緊雨。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 m4 heoi3 paau2 bou6 zung6 jiu3 lok6 gan2 jyu5

rows.note: Use this when adding another item or point, especially after mentioning the first one.

example.english: The food at this restaurant is tasty, plus the service is good.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳啲嘢好食，仲有服務又好。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 je5 hou2 sik6 zung6 jau5 fuk6 mou6 jau6 hou2

rows.note: Use this when presenting one factor as added to another, often in an explanatory statement.

example.english: There was traffic today, plus it rained heavily, so I was late.
example.traditional: 今日塞車，加上落大雨，所以我遲到。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 sak1 ce1 gaa1 soeng6 lok6 daai6 jyu5 so2 ji5 ngo5 ci4 dou3

rows.note: Use this formal connector for introducing a separate additional point in writing.

example.english: Plus, this report will also analyze the issue of costs.
example.traditional: 此外，今次報告亦會分析成本問題。
example.jyutping: ci2 ngoi6 gam1 ci3 bou3 gou3 jik6 wui5 fan1 sik1 sing4 bun2 man6 tai4
